{"name": "3378368f-b9cd-481f-a861-cd966dfcd5fc", "singleVisual": {"visualType": "textbox", "objects": {"general": [{"properties": {"paragraphs": [{"textRuns": [{"value": "RESEARCH PLATFORM SUMMARY & EXECUTIVE BLUEPRINT

BarrierLens implements a multi-stage machine learning architecture analyzing individual, household, logistical, and health facility barriers across 724,115 women from the NFHS-5 survey in 36 States & UTs.

• Stage 1 (Barrier Classification): Evaluates Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, and XGBoost across 3 barrier domains.
• Stage 2 (Outcome Modeling): Predicts Women with Confirmed Unmet Family Planning Need (N = 466,859), achieving a top ROC-AUC of 0.6657.
• AI Explainability: SHAP game-theoretic feature attributions rank age, wealth, vulnerability, and barrier probabilities as top drivers.
• Segmentation: K-Means clustering identifies 2 population risk archetypes (High Vulnerability vs High Inclusion).", "style": {"fontFamily": "Segoe UI", "fontSize": "11pt", "color": "#1D3557"}}]}]}}]}}}
